name: Everyday Non-Stick Frying Pan 20cm
description: A light everyday pan for eggs, omelettes and quick reheats. The three-layer non-stick release means less oil and an easier wash-up, and the riveted stay-cool handle keeps its grip on a busy stove. Suitable for gas, electric and ceramic hobs.
altText: Everyday non-stick frying pan, 20 centimetres, viewed from above

name: Everyday Non-Stick Frying Pan 26cm
description: The size most kitchens reach for first. Wide enough to brown four chicken thighs without crowding them, shallow enough to toss vegetables with one hand. Even heat across the base, and a rim shaped to pour without dripping.
altText: Everyday non-stick frying pan, 26 centimetres, on a wooden surface

name: Everyday Saucepan 16cm with Lid
description: A small workhorse for sauces, porridge and a single portion of rice. The tempered glass lid lets you watch a simmer without lifting it, and the encapsulated base stops milk catching on an electric plate.
altText: Stainless steel saucepan with glass lid, 16 centimetres

name: Everyday Saucepan 20cm with Lid
description: Three litres covers pasta for four, a batch of soup, or potatoes for a Sunday lunch. Graduated interior markings save you a measuring jug, and the handle is balanced so a full pan does not pull away from you.
altText: Stainless steel saucepan with glass lid, 20 centimetres

name: Everyday Stockpot 5L
description: Deep enough for stock, stews and a large pot of samp. Two solid side handles give you a proper grip when it is full and hot, and the base is thick enough to hold a low simmer for hours without scorching.
altText: Five litre stainless steel stockpot with two side handles

name: Signature Tri-Ply Frying Pan 28cm
material: Tri-ply stainless steel with aluminium core
description: Three bonded layers put an aluminium core between two sheets of stainless steel, so heat spreads to the edges instead of pooling in the middle. Takes a hard sear, deglazes cleanly, and goes into the oven to 240 degrees.
altText: Tri-ply stainless steel frying pan, 28 centimetres, with a long handle

name: Signature Tri-Ply Saucepan 18cm
material: Tri-ply stainless steel with aluminium core
description: The pan for anything that splits if you rush it: hollandaise, custard, a reduction you have spent an hour building. Gentle, even heat and a heavy lid that sits flush enough to hold steam.
altText: Tri-ply stainless steel saucepan with lid, 18 centimetres

name: Signature Sauté Pan 24cm with Lid
material: Tri-ply stainless steel with aluminium core
description: Straight sides and a wide flat base: brown first, add liquid, put the lid on and leave it. The one pan that handles a risotto, a curry and a braise without moving anything to a second dish.
altText: Stainless steel sauté pan with straight sides and a lid

name: Signature Carbon Steel Wok 30cm
description: Light enough to toss, thin enough to react the moment you turn the heat down. Arrives pre-seasoned and builds its own non-stick patina with use. Flat-bottomed, so it sits properly on a domestic hob.
altText: Carbon steel wok, 30 centimetres, with a wooden handle

name: Signature Ribbed Grill Pan 26cm
description: Deep ribs hold the meat clear of its own juices, which is the difference between a grilled steak and a boiled one. Heavy cast iron holds temperature when cold food hits it, and the marks it leaves are the real thing.
altText: Cast iron ribbed grill pan with searing ridges

name: Signature Stockpot 7L
material: Tri-ply stainless steel with aluminium core
description: Seven litres for stock, preserves and cooking for a crowd. The tri-ply base runs right up the walls, so the sides do not scorch when you reduce something down over a long afternoon.
altText: Seven litre tri-ply stainless steel stockpot

name: Signature Tri-Ply 5-Piece Set
material: Tri-ply stainless steel with aluminium core
description: The 18cm and 20cm saucepans, the 24cm sauté pan, the 28cm frying pan and a 7L stockpot, with lids. Everything in the range that earns its place in a working kitchen, bought once.
altText: Five piece tri-ply stainless steel cookware set arranged together

name: Heritage Cast Iron Casserole 24cm
description: Enamelled cast iron that goes from the hob to the oven to the table. Holds a low, even heat for the six hours a shin of beef actually needs, and the self-basting lid returns condensed steam to the dish rather than losing it.
altText: Enamelled cast iron casserole dish with lid, 24 centimetres

name: Heritage Cast Iron Casserole 28cm
description: The larger casserole, sized for a whole chicken or a lamb shoulder. Same enamel, same lid, more room. Heavy, deliberately so, and guaranteed for a lifetime of ordinary domestic use.
altText: Large enamelled cast iron casserole dish with lid, 28 centimetres

name: Heritage Cast Iron Skillet 26cm
description: Pre-seasoned bare cast iron with a pouring lip on each side. Gets hotter than a non-stick pan is ever allowed to, which is the whole point. Improves with every use and can be restored indefinitely.
altText: Seasoned cast iron skillet with pouring lips, 26 centimetres

name: Heritage Potjie Pot No. 3
description: Three legs, a wire bail handle and a lid that seals under its own weight. Built for coals rather than a hob, and sized for eight to ten people. Pre-seasoned, and it will outlast the person who buys it.
altText: Three legged cast iron potjie pot with wire handle and lid

name: Heritage Roasting Tin 38cm
description: Deep sides for fat and juices, and corners you can actually scrape a gravy out of. Hard-anodised so it will not warp at high oven temperatures, with integrated handles that stay reachable in a crowded oven.
altText: Hard anodised aluminium roasting tin with deep sides

name: Everyday Springform Baking Tin 24cm
description: A clamp-sided tin for cheesecakes and anything too fragile to turn out. The base sits proud of the ring so it releases cleanly, and the coating survives a dishwasher if you must.
altText: Non-stick springform baking tin with clamp, 24 centimetres

name: Signature Stovetop Kettle 1.7L
description: A stovetop kettle with a whistle you can hear from another room and a handle that folds back out of the steam. Wide base for fast boiling on gas or induction.
altText: Stainless steel stovetop whistling kettle

name: Heritage Copper Mixing Bowl 28cm
description: Unlined copper, which reacts with egg white to give a denser, more stable foam than glass or steel ever will. A specialist's bowl: hand wash, dry immediately, and it will patina into something worth keeping.
altText: Unlined copper mixing bowl with rolled rim, 28 centimetres
